title: Priority Encoder
body:
An [[Encoder]] that copes with more than one input being asserted at once: it outputs the
index of the **highest-priority** active input, and usually a "valid" bit saying whether
anything was active at all. A plain encoder given two simultaneous inputs produces
nonsense; a priority encoder produces an answer.

| $I_3 I_2 I_1 I_0$ | Out | |
|:-:|:-:|---|
| 0001 | 00 | |
| 001× | 01 | $I_1$ wins over $I_0$ |
| 01×× | 10 | |
| 1××× | 11 | $I_3$ beats everything |

This is precisely what the [[PIC]] needs. Several devices can raise an
[[IRQs|IRQ]] in the same cycle, and something has to decide which one the [[CPU]] services
first. The priority encoder turns the set of pending request lines into a single
[[IPL|interrupt priority level]], which then gets compared against the
[[Interrupt Mask]] and, if it wins, indexes the [[Vector Tables|vector table]].
